page: OVHcloud b3-8 is a general-purpose virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. The instance features 2 dedicated physical cores running at 2.3 GHz with a single thread per core, providing 2 vCPUs. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the instance in the top 25% of its class. However, multi-core CPU performance drops to average, and overall PassMark CPU and memory scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show a weak read-only speed for small cached blocks, though large-block uncached read and write operations maintain average speeds. Under database and web-serving workloads, the instance demonstrates limitations, with Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput scoring in the weak and poor categories respectively.

The b3-8 instance offers a balanced resource density for entry-level general-purpose workloads, delivering dedicated CPU resources without hyperthreading. This dedicated allocation provides predictable single-threaded execution, but the low overall memory bandwidth and weak multi-threaded decompression performance represent significant tradeoffs. Given these characteristics, the instance is suited for lightweight applications, basic utility scripting, single-threaded processing tasks, and small-scale development environments rather than high-throughput web serving or memory-intensive database operations.
